title: Line Extensions and New Service Construction: Contribution Standing Across a Member's Projects
content:
Before construction is scheduled on any **Line Extensions and New Service Construction** project, Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative reads the member's other projects.

## Rule

Construction may be scheduled only when no other project of the member carries a past-due contribution installment, the basis being the member's open contributions and the installment schedule of each project; the member's final-billed service balances are read under the Electric Service by Rate Schedule rules before the new service account is opened.

**The member's open contributions** are, at the point in time construction is to be scheduled and across every project of the member, the total of the contribution still due on each of the member's projects that is in contract signed, scheduled or energized status.

## Basis of the judgement

- **What is read.** The member's other construction projects, their status, the contribution still due on each, and the installment schedule of each project.
- **Whose projects.** Every project held by the same member, whatever its location or class of extension.
- **Authority.** The cooperative's own project records, read before construction is scheduled. The judgement rests on what those records show, not on the member's account of the other projects.
- **Effect.** A past-due contribution installment on any other project of the member bars scheduling construction on this project.

## Condition, judgement and result

| What the member's other projects show (hypothetical) | Past-due contribution installment on another project | Result under this rule |
|---|---|---|
| No other projects | No | This rule does not bar scheduling |
| One other project, energized, contribution paid in full | No | This rule does not bar scheduling |
| One other project, energized, installments invoiced and each paid when due | No | This rule does not bar scheduling |
| One other project, scheduled, one installment invoiced and now past due | Yes | Construction may not be scheduled |
| Two other projects, one current and one with a past-due installment | Yes | Construction may not be scheduled |

"Does not bar scheduling" means only that this rule is satisfied.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A hypothetical farm member holds an energized Farm and Ranch Extension project for a pivot, paying its contribution in monthly installments, and now has a new home project ready to schedule. The open contributions are read across both projects. If the pivot project's installment schedule shows an installment past due, construction on the home project may not be scheduled; if every invoiced installment on the pivot project has been paid as scheduled, this rule does not stand in the way.
